subject: Vendr profile attribute normalization request — TruNovo CAIQ/SIG mapping
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@vendrsecurity.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendr profile attribute normalization request — TruNovo CAIQ/SIG mapping

Hi Karthik / Camila,

Thanks for taking this on. When we ingested TruNovo's vendor profile we detected a set of inconsistent attribute values that are preventing their Vendr profile from lining up to the CAIQ fields customers expect (examples: CAIQ boolean fields present as free-text in "hosting_details", and multi-value controls split across different attributes).

I've attached a small diff (vendr-attribute-diff.csv) that shows the fields Vendr currently stores vs. the canonical CAIQ/SIG keys our buyers look for. There's also a short sample mapping (trunovo-caiq-mapping-sample.pdf) that illustrates how customers typically surface these attributes on the portal.

Could you confirm two things so we can proceed with a one-off normalization pass?
- Which internal attribute names at Redwood should be treated as canonical for mapping (e.g. "sso_present", "kms_key_rotation", "third_party_hosting")?
- Are there any programmatic constraints (e.g. only boolean values, or limited enumerations) we should enforce when we rewrite the Vendr attributes?

If easier, we can hop on a 20-minute call — propose Thu 8/26 11:00 AM PT. Otherwise a short reply with the canonical field list is fine and we'll push the changes and share a final diff.

Attachments: vendr-attribute-diff.csv, trunovo-caiq-mapping-sample.pdf

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Vendor Success — Vendr Security Operations

Subject: Re: Vendr profile attribute normalization request — TruNovo CAIQ/SIG mapping

Thanks Sarah — and hi Camila / Laura.

We ran a quick pass on the attached diff and the ask makes sense. High-level constraints from our side:
- Canonical booleans: sso_present, kms_rotation, external_hosting. If a source field is free-text, prefer converting to boolean where the text is an explicit yes/no; otherwise tag as "unknown" and follow up.
- Enumerations: for encryption at rest we use {none, partial, full}.
- We prefer not to change historical evidence pointers (S3 links and SOC2 attachments) as part of attribute normalization; that needs a separate evidence upload flow.

I'll send our internal template back (redwood-vendr-attr-template.csv) with the canonical names filled for TruNovo and Camila can help confirm mappings. If Vendr needs an API payload format, point us at the expected schema and we'll prepare it.

I'm fine with Thu 8/26 11:00 AM PT — confirm the calendar invite and I'll add Laura to take the evidence handoff items.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-vendr-attr-template.csv
